children: Ed Yardeni cut his year-end S&P 500 (
target to 7,900 from 8,400, citing rising bond yields and increasing downside risks over the next three to six months, Bloomberg reported.
The new target represents a 4.1% gain from the S&P 500's Tuesday close and marks a reversal from Yardeni's August upgrade, when he raised his forecast to 8,400 from 8,250, Bloomberg reported.

Yardeni, president and chief investment strategist of Yardeni Research, also lowered his year-end forward price-to-earnings estimate for the S&P 500 to 18.6 from 19.8. He said in a client note that the recent rise in bond yields prompted the lower valuation assumption and target.
The move comes as other strategists have also turned more cautious on the index. Wells Fargo cut its year-end S&P 500 target to 7,700 from 7,950,
the index had limited upside from current levels and could initially fall 5%-10% as the earnings cycle enters its late stages.

Wells Fargo analyst Ohsung Kwon said the team had become more cautious heading into September even as it raised its earnings forecasts to $425 for 2027 and $460 for 2028. The firm expects multiple compressions to offset some of that earnings strength.

Yardeni remains constructive on the longer-term outlook, with his S&P 500 target for the end of the decade unchanged at 10,000, Bloomberg reported. He also expects the U.S. economy to expand without entering a recession through the end of the decade.
The 8,400 target Yardeni previously set is now effectively his mid-2027 target, while his 2027 earnings-per-share forecast remains at $425, the report stated.

With the Federal Reserve's September rate decision due Wednesday, Yardeni has also warned that a combination of higher inflation and slower growth would be particularly challenging for stocks, Bloomberg reported.

title: Yardeni cuts S&P 500 target to 7,900 on rising yields
